source.pdf: purchased pattern PDF, 12 pages, text extracted with pypdf (not in the repository)

product_type.value: cardigan with pockets, open front, no closure

value.body: one piece worked flat side to side: first front, chained sleeve opening, back, chained sleeve opening, second front; hem ribbing worked into every body row
value.sleeves: worked separately side to side, folded lengthways and seamed; sewn to the armholes
value.neckline_ribbing: worked separately, sewn along the entire neckline
value.pockets: worked separately, sewn to the front panels (optional, make 2)
value.seams: whip stitch, right sides in, wrong side facing out

value.name: Crumpled Waffle Stitch / Textured HDC
value.row_2: ch1, (BLO hdc, FLO hdc) repeated, hdc in last
value.row_3: ch1, (FLO hdc, BLO hdc) repeated, hdc in last

value.cuff_stitch: slip stitch in back loop (rows B) / hdc BLO (rows A)
value.finish: fold in half lengthways, whip stitch the edges together

value.row: ch1, BLO hdc 6, hdc in last

value.top_edge: slip-stitch edging along a row-end edge (rows run vertically on the garment)
value.placement: UNKNOWN in the text: 'try on the cardigan to double-check pocket placement'; sewn through the front panel only

value: fronts laid on back, whip stitch shoulder seams

pin and whip stitch pockets to the front panels

warnings: WARNING ASSEMBLY_UNPLACED: assembly steps [3, 4, 5] join two different pieces without saying where on the second piece the join happens. A maker can follow every round and still not know where the ears go

assembly.why: 2 of 5 joins do not name their edges, so the object's shape is only partly determined

joins.why: self-seam: one piece folded and closed

body.why: the loop target changes along the row and changes again on the next row, so no column persists: the surface breaks up rather than running in ridges
body.orientation_is_in_fabric_axes: along/up the rows, not up/across the worn garment. Which of those is vertical depends on the panel's grain direction, which the CIR does not carry, so this deliberately does not say

sleeve.why: the loop target changes along the row and changes again on the next row, so no column persists: the surface breaks up rather than running in ridges
sleeve.orientation_is_in_fabric_axes: along/up the rows, not up/across the worn garment. Which of those is vertical depends on the panel's grain direction, which the CIR does not carry, so this deliberately does not say

neckband.why: the loop target is the same everywhere, so every row leaves its unworked loop in the same place and the rows stack into ridges: this is ribbing
neckband.orientation_is_in_fabric_axes: along/up the rows, not up/across the worn garment. Which of those is vertical depends on the panel's grain direction, which the CIR does not carry, so this deliberately does not say
